title: When the Archive Falls Anew
premise: Bram Villalobos smuggles forbidden memory-records out of Meridian Station, an orbital colony officially declared abandoned after the war between Earth's Concord and the Outer Reach began. When a derelict ship returns from deep space carrying its crew aged backward into children, Bram discovers they carry a recorded peace treaty the Concord buried to justify the war. Hunted by customs enforcers and betrayed by his own lover, a Concord intelligence officer, Bram must choose between erasing the evidence and saving himself, or broadcasting the truth and dooming the colony that sheltered him. He broadcasts it — at the cost of the station and nearly his own life — forcing both sides to the table as the archive falls anew.
about_author: Theo Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to signals no one answered. They write science fiction about people who keep records when keeping records is dangerous.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: POV Bram. A routine smuggling run through orbital customs goes wrong when inspectors scan too deep, forcing Bram to hide a dying colonist's memory-record inside his own neural implant. The chapter establishes Meridian's forgotten suffering and Bram's quiet code: he carries what others want erased. Emotional beat: weary defiance, the loneliness of being the only witness.

chapters.title: The Ship That Came Home Young
chapters.summary: POV Bram. The Halcyon drifts back after eleven years missing, its crew aged backward into children who speak in fragments of a treaty signing no one remembers. Customs seals the wreck; Bram, tipped off by an old contact, sneers at the official story but can't resist one dive into the hold. Emotional beat: uncanny dread giving way to wonder — history has come home wearing smaller faces.

chapters.title: What the Children Remember
chapters.summary: POV Sefa, a child crew member. Through fragmented memories, Sefa recalls her adult self witnessing the Concord reject a peace accord and order the Halcyon silenced. She trusts Bram because he listens without flinching. Meanwhile Concord agents arrive asking questions with guns behind them. Emotional beat: innocence weaponized; the horror of remembering a future you never got to live.

chapters.title: Officer Ilsa Reyes
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa, Bram's lover and a Concord intelligence officer. Ordered to locate the 'anomalous minors,' she realizes Bram is entangled and must decide whether to warn him or use him. Their reunion crackles with tenderness laced with mutual suspicion. Emotional beat: love against duty — she chooses him for now, knowing the choice has a clock on it.

chapters.title: The Buried Accord
chapters.summary: POV Bram. Decoding the Halcyon's hidden data-core with a disgraced archivist named Oyelaran, Bram confirms the treaty exists in full — and that ending the war would expose every official who profited from it. Enforcers raid the archive district; Oyelaran dies buying time. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve; truth stops being abstract and starts costing blood.

chapters.title: Invisible No Longer
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Her superiors deduce Bram holds the core and order her to retrieve it or be charged as a collaborator. She feeds him a false escape window instead, crossing a line she can't uncross. Bram realizes she's sacrificed herself to buy him hours. Emotional beat: betrayal inverted into loyalty; the terrible intimacy of being saved by someone you expected to lose.

chapters.title: Running the Silent Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Bram. With Sefa and the core aboard a patched-together freighter, Bram runs the war's dead zone while Concord hunters and Reach privateers both close in. A near-fatal ambush forces him to jettison his own collected memories — years of the colony's testimony — to lighten the ship. Emotional beat: sacrifice of self; he becomes the message instead of its messenger.

chapters.title: The Price of the Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. At the Reach relay station, they find the only transmitter strong enough, guarded by soldiers who want the war ended but fear what peace will reveal. Sefa, using her doubled memories, convinces them. As the broadcast begins, Concord strike ships enter orbit above Meridian. Emotional beat: trembling hope; children teaching adults how to stop being afraid.

chapters.title: When the Archive Falls
chapters.summary: POV Bram. The treaty floods every open channel as Meridian burns under bombardment. Ilsa, court-martialed and defiant, refuses the order to jam the signal and transmits the Concord's own internal proof alongside it. Bram, wounded, watches the station that raised him fall — and watches fleets on both sides go silent mid-fire. Emotional beat: devastation fused with vindication; the cost made visible.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: POV Bram, months later. Armistice talks proceed in the shadow of Meridian's wreckage; survivors rebuild the archive openly, and Sefa leads the returned crew home to families who barely recognize them. Ilsa arrives under white flag, and Bram must decide whether love can survive having been a weapon. He lets her stay. Emotional beat: cautious grace; justice achieved outside the law, and loyalty chosen over bitterness.
